subjects.displayTitle: Serving humanity: from compassion to collective progress
subjects.introduction: Every person, Bahá’u’lláh says, has been called into being for the betterment of the world. The claim turns ordinary life inside out: a bed offered to a stranger, a wound dressed, a sorrowful friend made glad, become what a human being exists to do. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls such service worship, the physician at a sickbed giving praise as surely as anyone at prayer. The circle then widens past family and friend to opponent and foreigner, and past the single act to schools, honest public office, science and the patient building of institutions that leave people more capable. Service tests the server too, asking humility, freedom from the wish for praise, care for the dignity of the one helped, and perseverance when humanity proves ungrateful. The Samaritan who becomes a neighbour by acting, and Krishna’s summons to work for the good of the world, press the question from other traditions. The road leads into kindness to the poor and the sick, into useful work and a craft practised with conscience, and into the ascent of a civilization at once material and spiritual.
subjects.arc: An ordinary act, a worldwide responsibility → Who belongs within our concern? → Care that protects dignity → A life of worship in action → Education opens possibilities → Peace and the ethics of public action → The worker is also transformed → A purpose carried through history → Hope becomes a shared undertaking → Communities learn to act together

order.why: Begin with the startling claim that every person has been created for the betterment of the world.
shortened: All men have been called into being for the betterment of the world. It behoveth every soul to arise and serve his brethren for the sake of God.

order.why: Immediately give that claim a human face: shelter, healing, food, consolation, and dignity.
Complicate good intentions with the need to understand what this particular age requires.
shortened: The remedy the world needeth in its present-day afflictions can never be the same as that which a subsequent age may require. Be anxiously concerned with the needs of the age ye live in, and centre your deliberations on its exigencies and requirements.

Gaze ye therein and be apprised thereof; perchance ye may be aided thereby to recognize the Friend and may be not the cause of His displeasure. In this Day the choicest fruit of the tree of knowledge is that which serveth the welfare of humanity and safeguardeth its interests.

order.why: Expand the scale from individual kindness to learning, laws, institutions, and the happiness of every member of society.
shortened: And the honor and distinction of the individual consist in this, that he among all the world's multitudes should become a source of social good. Is any larger bounty conceivable than this, that an individual, looking within himself, should find that by the confirming grace of God he has become the cause of peace and well-being, of happiness and advantage to his fellow men?

The primary purpose, the basic objective, in laying down powerful laws and setting up great principles and institutions dealing with every aspect of civilization, is human happiness; and human happiness consists only in drawing closer to the Threshold of Almighty God, and in securing the peace and well-being of every individual member, high and low alike, of the human race; and the supreme agencies for accomplishing these two objectives are the excellent qualities with which humanity has been endowed.

order.why: Ask whether the reader’s words have become a patient life of active service.
shortened: Without action nothing in the material world can be accomplished, neither can words unaided advance a man in the spiritual Kingdom. It is not through lip-service only that the elect of God have attained to holiness, but by patient lives of active service they have brought light into the world.

order.why: Distinguish a benevolence confined to selected people from an intention embracing all created things.
shortened: In the world of creation, good intentions are of two kinds. One kind is particular and aimed at specific people; this is limited and its scope is extremely narrow. The other kind is directed towards all created things; it is all-pervading and extensive in range.

order.why: Let the image of a physician introduce service itself as a form of prayer.
shortened: This is worship: to serve mankind and to minister to the needs of the people. Service is prayer. A physician ministering to the sick, gently, tenderly, free from prejudice and believing in the solidarity of the human race, he is giving praise'.

order.why: Join insight to action and place the preceding acts of care within the citizenship of one world.
shortened: It is incumbent upon every man of insight and understanding to strive to translate that which hath been written into reality and action.

That one indeed is a man who, today, dedicateth himself to the service of the entire human race.  The Great Being saith:	Blessed and happy is he that ariseth to promote the best interests of the peoples and kindreds of the earth.  In another passage He hath proclaimed:  It is not for him to pride himself who loveth his own country, but rather for him who loveth the whole world.  The earth is but one country, and mankind its citizens.

Look not upon any limitations and be not restricted by any bonds, for limitations and restrictions become dark veils preventing the manifestation of human perfections, while freedom causes the appearance of divine bounties.

It signifieth education for all mankind, guidance for all men, the spreading far and wide of the sweet savours of the spirit, the promulgation of God's proofs, the setting forth of arguments conclusive and divine, the doing of charitable deeds.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: They are awake and vigilant, they shun the obscurity of the world of nature, their highest wish centereth on the eradication from among men of the struggle for existence, the shining forth of the spirituality and the love of the realm on high, the exercise of utmost kindness among peoples, the realization of an intimate and close connection between religions and the practice of the ideal of self-sacrifice. Then will the world of humanity be transformed into the Kingdom of God.
At least engage ye in a deed of profit to the world of humanity that ye may partially compensate for that loss.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: May they arise to fulfill the divine teachings and contemplate peace and reconciliation with all the peoples of the world. May each become a kind servant to the human world and a loving friend to all humanity.

shortened: Today the world of humanity is in need of the improvement of character, education through the divine breaths, and the establishment of the foundation of love, truthfulness, peace, reconciliation, reality, uprightness and fellowship among all members of humankind. We must serve this vital cause. Other matters have no importance. Interference in governmental affairs and discourse about them has no significance, for the important matter is that which we promote: the illumination and comfort and tranquility of all creation. Is it permissible that we should falter in this and occupy ourselves with other matters? No, by God!

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: They must be truthful and kind to all the peoples of the world, deal with all humanity with pure intent, absolute benevolence and heartfelt love, be sincere and well-wishing toward all the governments of the world, and, in accordance with Baha'u'llah's testament, never interfere in political matters - indeed, not even discuss them.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: This preservation, protection, security and comfort was due to the blessing of the sacred teachings, whereby the friends of God in no region interfered in political affairs, but rather spent their time in supplication and prayer, turning to the glorious Kingdom, striving for the good of all, serving humanity, experiencing spiritual attractions and divine inspirations.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.

order.why: Test public office by its purpose: public good or personal advantage.
shortened: If the object is to promote the public good, then the president must be a well-wisher of all and not a self-seeking person. If the object, however, is to promote personal interests, then such a position will be injurious to humanity and not beneficial to the public.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: Convey my utmost kindness to your brother and tell him that in whatever government department he becomes employed, he should not rest day or night but rather serve the government and nation, demonstrate the utmost truthfulness, honesty, trustworthiness, purity and nobility, be content with his salary however small it may be, and be free and sanctified from all defilement - so that it may become evident that the Baha'is are heavenly angels who have no desire except service to humanity, especially to their homeland.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.

On behalf of this servant convey perfect love and yearning greetings to his honor the late Qamarof and say that we are always engaged in prayer for you, that God may confirm and assist you to be successful in great matters in service to that just king, to render outstanding services, and to leave an eternal trace in the world of humanity.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: To attain to true glory and honour, man should exercise justice and equity, forbear to act in an oppressive manner, render service to his government, and work for the good of his fellow-citizens.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.
shortened: The point is that the Baha'is are servants of the human world and captivated by justice and wisdom, well-wishers of the world's leaders, enchanted by radiant countenance and attracted to the character of well-wishers.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.

Should the leaders of government and nation manifest spiritual virtues, goodly deeds, and kindly words, the lights of justice will encompass all the earth, and all will dwell in perfect tranquility within the pavilion of security and peace. The foundation of the security and welfare of nations rests upon two pillars: reward and punishment. Every sovereign must implement these two principles; indeed it is essential.

Do not busy yourselves in your own concerns; let your thoughts be fixed upon that which will rehabilitate the fortunes of mankind and sanctify the hearts and souls of men. This can best be achieved through pure and holy deeds, through a virtuous life and a goodly behaviour. Valiant acts will ensure the triumph of this Cause, and a saintly character will reinforce its power.

order.why: Extend service into cooperation and public responsibility, holding honest administration and peaceful means beside cautions about political involvement and self-interest.

Bend your minds and wills to the education of the peoples and kindreds of the earth, that haply the dissensions that divide it may, through the power of the Most Great Name, be blotted out from its face, and all mankind become the upholders of one Order, and the inhabitants of one City.

The indispensability of this coherence is unmistakably illustrated in His ordination of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, the spiritual centre of every Baha'i community round which must flourish dependencies dedicated to the social, humanitarian, educational and scientific advancement of mankind.

shortened: As the Movement extends the bounds of its influence and its opportunities for fuller recognition multiply, the twofold character of the obligations imposed on its National elected representatives should, I feel, be increasingly emphasized. shortened: Social and economic development is an important area of activity in and of itself. Its justification should not be sought in its ability to produce enrollments; it complements teaching and also contributes to it.

order.why: Shift the question from doing something for a population to strengthening its own capacity to act.
shortened: ...while social action may involve the provision of goods and services in some form, its primary concern must be to build capacity within a given population to participate in creating a better world. Social change is not a project that one group of people carries out for the benefit of another. The scope and complexity of social action must be commensurate with the human resources available in a village or neighbourhood to carry it forward. Efforts best begin, then, on a modest scale and grow organically as capacity within the population develops.

shortened: Secondly, we must always bear in mind that there are so few Baha'is in the world, relative to the world's population, and so many people in need, that even if all of us gave all we had, it would not alleviate more than an infinitesimal amount of suffering. This does not mean we must not help the needy, we should; but our contributions to the Faith are the surest way of lifting once and for all time the burden of hunger and misery from mankind, for it is only through the System of Baha'u'llah--Divine in origin--that the world can be gotten on its feet, and want, fear, hunger, war, etc., be eliminated.

order.why: Close with an acknowledgment of continuing suffering, leaving room for humility about both its meaning and the limits of our understanding.
shortened: As long as there will be life on earth, there will also be suffering, in various forms and degrees. But suffering, although an inescapable reality, can nevertheless be utilized as a means for the attainment of happiness. This is the interpretation given to it by all the Prophets and saints, who, in the midst of severe tests and trials, felt happy and joyous and experienced what is best and holiest in life. Suffering is both a reminder and a guide.
God's wisdom is, indeed, inscrutable to us all, and it is no use pushing too far trying to discover that which shall always remain a mystery to our mind.

questions: How does the claim that everyone is created for the betterment of the world change the meaning of an ordinary act of care, a profession, or a public responsibility?
Which passages most challenge the limits of your concern for others? What would service across those limits require in practice, especially where there is prejudice or hostility?
How do relief of immediate suffering, education, spiritual growth, and the improvement of institutions support one another? Where might an imbalance among them become harmful?

What distinguishes service that protects dignity and builds people’s own capacity from service that makes them dependent on a benefactor? How do the passages on humility, intention, and learning help you make that distinction?
What do the Samaritan’s care and the Gita’s account of exemplary action bring into focus here? How do their distinctive religious settings affect the comparison?
What modest undertaking could a group begin in response to a real local need, and how could it learn from those involved while sustaining health, joy, and perseverance?
